## What’s next in AI:7 trends to watch in 2026

by Susanna Ray

AI is entering a new phase, one defined by real-world impact.

After several years of experimentation, 2026 is shaping up to be the year AI evolves from instrument to partner, transforming how we work, create and solve problems. Across industries, AI is moving beyond answering questions to collaborating with people and amplifying their expertise.

This transformation is visible everywhere. In medicine, AI is helping close gaps in care. In software development, it’s learning not just code but the context behind it. In scientific research, it’s becoming a true lab assistant. In quantum computing, new hybrid approaches are heralding breakthroughs once thought impossible. [...] As AI agents become digital colleagues and take on specific tasks at human direction, organizations are strengthening security to keep pace with new risks. supporting_texts.text:
Another emerging trend is the growing collaboration between humans and AI systems. Rather than replacing human workers, many AI technologies are designed to augment human capabilities. AI can process enormous amounts of data, identify patterns, and generate insights that support better decision-making. Humans, on the other hand, provide creativity, judgment, and contextual understanding. In many industries, the most effective solutions will involve collaboration between human expertise and AI-powered analysis. [...] Artificial intelligence is gradually becoming one of the foundational technologies of the digital age, comparable to the impact of the internet or mobile computing. Its applications already extend across healthcare, transportation, education, finance, entertainment, and scientific research. As AI systems become more capable, they will likely open new opportunities for innovation, productivity, and discovery.

fusionai_answer.answer_text:
Current trends in AI include multi-modal AI, autonomous agents, and ethical AI development, with a focus on edge computing, AI democratization, and real-time decision-making [Evidence 1]. These trends are expected to continue in 2026, with an increased focus on explainable and ethical AI, as well as the integration of AI in wearables and smart devices [Evidence 3]. Additionally, conversational AI is becoming more sophisticated, with context-aware assistants that can understand intent, tone, and emotion, enhancing customer experience and productivity [Evidence 2]. The rise of customized models is also a key trend, with organizations using proprietary datasets to train AI tailored to their specific needs, and companies investing in data quality assurance to maintain AI performance and ethical robustness [Evidence 4]. Furthermore, AI is being used in various industries, including gaming, where it is being used to create more immersive and engaging experiences [Evidence 7]. However, there are also concerns about the impact of AI on society, with some people embracing AI and others being more skeptical [Evidence 5].

Key findings: Multi-modal AI, autonomous agents, and ethical AI development are key trends in AI; Conversational AI is becoming more sophisticated and context-aware; Customized models are on the rise, with organizations using proprietary datasets to train AI; AI is being used in various industries, including gaming; There are concerns about the impact of AI on society

Related follow-up searches: AI systems; Anthropic; Arnav et al.; Baker et al.; DiffusionGemma; Emmons et al.

Limitations: The evidence is limited to 2026 and may not reflect future trends; The evidence is focused on specific industries and may not be generalizable to all industries
